name: ManagedAppDistribution
summary: Manage the distribution of apps within an organization.

declarations.name: ManagedApp
declarations.comment:
A representation of a managed app.

``ManagedApp`` represents a managed app that the framework can install. Use an instance of this object to obtain
information about the app.

members.comment: The app's localized description.

members.name: releaseDate
members.comment: The app's release date.

members.name: releaseNotes
members.comment: The app's localized developer release notes.

members.name: requirements
members.comment: The app's localized operating system compatibility requirements.

members.name: contentRating
members.comment: The app's content age rating.

members.name: privacyPolicy
members.comment: The app's privacy policy URL.

members.name: screenshotURLs
members.comment:
An array of the app's screenshot URLs.

The screenshots scale to fit the given size.

- Parameter size: The size of the screenshots.
- Returns: The URLs of the screenshots.

members.name: developerWebsite
members.comment: The app's developer website URL.

members.name: licenseAgreement

members.name: metadataLanguage

members.name: id

members.name: name
members.comment: The app's localized name.

members.name: genres

members.name: seller

members.name: iconURL
members.comment:
A URL for the icon of the app.

The icon scales to fit the given size.
- Parameter size: The size of the icon.
- Returns: The URL of the icon.

members.name: version
members.comment: The app's version information.

members.name: fileSize
members.comment: The size of the app in bytes.

members.name: platform
members.comment: The platform of the app.

members.name: subtitle
members.comment: The app's localized subtitle.

members.name: copyright
members.comment: The app's copyright information.

members.name: languages
members.comment:
The app's supported languages.
> Tip: Use ``Locale.localizedString(forLanguageCode:)`` to obtain a display name for the language, using ``metadataLanguage``  to create the ``Locale``.

This appears in the body of an alert.

members.name: attemptRecovery
members.signature: func attemptRecovery(optionIndex recoveryOptionIndex: Int, resultHandler handler: @escaping (Bool) -> Void)
members.comment:
Attempt to recover from this error when someone selects the option at the given index.

- Parameters:
    - optionIndex: An index into ``recoveryOptions``.
    - resultHandler: A closure that the method calls with the recovery status.

- Returns: A recovery handler with the recovery status.

members.name: attemptRecovery
members.comment:
Attempt to recover from this error when someone selects the option at the given index.

- Parameters:
    - optionIndex: An index into ``recoveryOptions``.

- Returns: `true` to indicate successful recovery; otherwise `false`.

members.comment: A set of possible recovery options to present.

members.name: errorDescription
members.comment:

This appears in the title of an alert.

members.name: recoverySuggestion
members.comment: A suggestion for recovering from the error.

members.name: localizedStringResource

declarations.name: ManagedAppLibrary
declarations.comment: A representation of a library of managed apps.

members.name: availableApps
members.comment:
The current managed apps available to this device.

The current managed apps are of type `Result<[ManagedApp], ManagedAppDistributionError>`. Use an
asynchronous `for` loop to update your views when the current managed apps change.
If the device can't retrieve the metadata for the apps, fetching the list of managed apps fails with ``ManagedAppDistributionError.networkError``. An example of this failure is if the device is offline.

> Note: The async sequence returns an error and the sequence ends when running as an iOS app on macOS.

members.name: currentDistributor
members.comment:
The library provider for managed apps on this device.

This is a singleton object.

declarations.name: ManagedAppLibrary.ManagedApps
declarations.comment: An array of managed apps that updates as apps become available or unavailable.
